description: Exchange-level chunks from past voice conversations (one user turn plus Blau's reply, the chunk shape LongMemEval recommends and #62 indexes). Topics recur across conversations, so each query has to find the one exchange that holds the detail.

documents.text: User: We finally booked the flights to Japan. We land in Tokyo on April 2nd and fly home from Osaka on the 16th. Blau: Two weeks is a good length. Spring is cherry blossom season, so book hotels soon; Kyoto fills up first.

User: Alex wants three nights in Kyoto and I want to see Naoshima for the art museums. Blau: Naoshima is a day trip from Okayama, so you could stop there on the way from Kyoto to Osaka without adding a hotel night.

User: Is the JR Pass still worth it for our route? Blau: After the 2023 price rise, a 7-day pass costs more than Tokyo to Kyoto and Kyoto to Osaka bought separately. For your route, individual shinkansen tickets are cheaper.

User: Remember that ramen place my friend recommended in Osaka, the one with the yuzu shio broth? Blau: You said it's called Menya Kotori, near Namba station, and that it opens at 11 and sells out by 2.

User: I'm nervous about my shellfish allergy in Japan, so much of the food has dashi. Blau: Most dashi is kombu and bonito, which is fish, not shellfish, but some broths use shrimp or clams. Carry a printed allergy card in Japanese and show it every time you order.

User: We booked the ryokan in Kyoto, the one in Higashiyama with the private bath. Blau: Nice. Ryokan dinners are set menus, so send them your allergy in advance; most will adjust the kaiseki if they know a few days ahead.
User: Should we get a pocket wifi or an eSIM for Japan? Blau: Since you both have unlocked iPhones, an eSIM is simpler: nothing to pick up or return, and 20 GB each is plenty for two weeks of maps.
User: Alex wants to do a cooking class in Tokyo. Blau: A small market-tour class in Tsukiji would suit you both; ask them to swap any shellfish dishes before you book.

User: I signed up for the Oakland half marathon on November 8th. My goal is under two hours. Blau: That's about 9:09 per mile. With 18 weeks to go, a plan with three easy runs, one tempo run and one long run a week will get you there.

User: The outside of my right knee hurts after about six miles. Blau: Pain on the outside of the knee that starts at a predictable distance often points to the IT band. Cut the long run back a mile, add hip strengthening, and see a physical therapist if it lasts more than two weeks.

User: The physical therapist said it's IT band syndrome and gave me clamshells and side planks. Blau: Good news that it's not structural. Do the exercises daily, and keep long runs on flat routes for now; downhills make it worse.
User: Ran ten miles today with no knee pain at all, average pace 9:31. Blau: That's a big step. Your long-run pace should be slower than race pace, so 9:31 is right where it should be.

User: My running shoes have about 450 miles on them. Blau: Most shoes lose their cushioning between 300 and 500 miles. Buy the same model now and break them in on easy runs, so you don't race in new shoes.

User: What should I eat the morning of the race? Blau: Something you've already tested on long runs, about two to three hours before the start, like a bagel with peanut butter and a banana. Nothing new on race day.

User: The tempo run felt awful this morning, I couldn't hold 8:50. Blau: One bad tempo run usually means poor sleep or not enough food, not lost fitness. You slept five hours on Saturday; take an easy day and try again Thursday.
User: Should I taper before the half? Blau: Yes. Cut your weekly mileage by about 30% in the last ten days and keep a few short race-pace efforts so your legs stay sharp.

User: I want to hire a customer success lead but we can't afford one until the seed closes. Blau: You could write the job description now and start talking to candidates, so you can make an offer the week the money lands.
User: The ideal person has worked a restaurant floor. Blau: Then look at former general managers who moved into hospitality software sales. They know the pain and they've learned to use a CRM.

User: I talked to a candidate named Keisha who managed a brunch spot for eight years. She was great with the pilot owners. Blau: Ask her to run a mock onboarding call with Rosa from Little Fern; it's the closest thing to the real job.

User: Keisha's mock onboarding went really well, Rosa loved her. What salary should I offer? Blau: For an early customer success lead in the Bay Area, $95,000 to $110,000 base plus 0.3% to 0.5% equity is a reasonable range.

User: Priya thinks we should hire the second iOS engineer before customer success. Blau: The tie-breaker is what's slowing growth today. If onboarding is the bottleneck, customer success first; if Android requests are losing deals, the engineer.

User: I want to get to conversational Spanish before we visit Alex's family in Mexico City next summer. Blau: Daily practice beats long sessions. Fifteen minutes of app practice plus one hour a week with a tutor is a solid plan.
User: I found a tutor, Lucía, we meet Tuesdays at 7 pm on video. Blau: Great. Ask her to spend most of the hour on conversation; you can do grammar drills on your own.
User: I keep mixing up ser and estar. Blau: A simple rule: estar is for states and locations that can change, ser is for identity and lasting traits. Estoy cansado, but soy alto.
User: Lucía says my listening is behind my speaking. Blau: Try Spanish podcasts made for learners, like slow news, at normal speed on your runs. Listening during easy runs adds three hours a week.

User: I held a whole twenty-minute conversation with Lucía about the restaurant without switching to English. Blau: That's a real milestone. Talking about your own work is the hardest topic to stay in Spanish for.
User: Our lease ends January 31st and the landlord is raising rent to $3,650. Blau: That's a 12% increase. You have until December 1st to give notice, so you have about four months to compare.

User: We want to look in Rockridge so I can walk to BART and Alex can bike to work. Blau: Rockridge two-bedrooms list around $3,800 to $4,300. A one-bedroom plus an office nook might keep you under $3,600.

User: We saw a place on Lawton Avenue, two bedrooms, $3,900, but no in-unit laundry. Blau: Laundry matters more than people expect; budget about $60 a month and two hours a week for a laundromat if you take it.
User: The landlord on Lawton said dogs are okay but only under 40 pounds. Blau: Biscuit is 32 pounds, so he fits. Get the pet policy in writing in the lease.
User: We decided to renew our current place after all; they came down to $3,450. Blau: That saves you the move and is $450 a month less than Lawton. Ask for a two-year lease to lock it in.
User: Dad turns 70 on December 12th. I want to do something special. Blau: A milestone like that is often about people more than things. Could you gather the family somewhere meaningful to him?

User: Dad always talks about the fishing trips he took in the Sierra as a kid. Blau: A weekend at a cabin near the lake he went to, with everyone there, could be the gift. Book soon if it's near a holiday weekend.

User: Cabins near Lake Alpine close in winter because of snow. Blau: Then hold the cabin trip for June, and for his birthday give him a framed map of the lake with the trip dates and a note from everyone.
User: My sister Mei is collecting old photos of Dad for a slideshow at the birthday dinner. Blau: Ask relatives to send scans by mid-November so Mei has two weeks to put it together.
User: I just finished The Mom Test. Blau: Its main idea fits your work: ask restaurant owners about what they did last week, not whether they would use a feature.
User: Recommend a novel, something I can read before bed that isn't about startups. Blau: Try Klara and the Sun by Kazuo Ishiguro. It's quiet and short chapters make it easy to stop.
User: Klara and the Sun was beautiful, I cried at the end. Blau: If you liked its tone, The Remains of the Day by the same author is a good next one.

User: I'm reading a book on pricing called Monetizing Innovation. Blau: Its core advice is to design the product around willingness to pay before you build. It matches how you moved Larderly to tiers.

User: Marcus from Northgate said our seed deck needs a clearer story on why restaurants won't churn. Blau: Lead with the cohort chart: restaurants open more than two years have had zero product churn, and net revenue retention is 128%.

User: Should we raise the seed now or wait until we hit $25k MRR? Blau: At 22% monthly growth you'd reach $25k in about three months. Raising after that milestone usually means a better price, and you have 13 months of runway.

User: Had a first call with a seed fund called Bayline Capital. They asked about gross margin and the cost of the invoice model. Blau: Your 81% gross margin is solid. Mention the invoice model costs about 9 cents per invoice and drops as you fine-tune a smaller model.

User: Bayline wants a second meeting with Priya to go deep on the tech. Blau: Prepare Priya with the invoice mapping accuracy, 97.4% on 2,000 labelled invoices, and the plan to move more of it on device.

User: Dana thinks we should apply to YC before raising the seed. Blau: YC would add a demo day and a higher valuation, at the cost of 7% plus the standard deal. With 13 months of runway you can afford to apply for the winter batch first.

User: I want to meal prep lunches on Sundays so I stop eating chips at my desk. Blau: Pick one grain, one protein and two roasted vegetables each week and mix the sauces. Four lunches take about 90 minutes.

User: This week's prep was farro, chicken thighs, roasted broccoli and sweet potato with a tahini lemon sauce. Blau: That's a good balance. Farro holds up for four days in the fridge better than rice does.
User: Alex wants to try a vegetarian week. Blau: Swap the chicken for crispy chickpeas or marinated tofu; both keep well and the tahini sauce still works.
User: Can you give me a quick weeknight dinner without shellfish that Alex will like? Blau: Miso-glazed salmon with rice and bok choy takes 25 minutes, and there's no shellfish anywhere in it.
User: I keep waking up at 4 am thinking about work. Blau: Try writing tomorrow's top three tasks before bed so your brain can let go of them, and keep the phone out of the bedroom.
User: The to-do list before bed helped, I've slept through four nights in a row. Blau: Great. Keep the same wake-up time on weekends too; it's what anchors your sleep the most.
User: I've been having two coffees after lunch on hard days. Blau: Caffeine's half-life is five to six hours, so a 3 pm coffee is still half there at 9 pm. Try making the second one decaf.

User: Clover's partner program wants a demo of our integration before they list us. Blau: Build the demo with one pilot restaurant's real menu; their reviewers care most that items and modifiers sync correctly.

User: Tomás found that Clover reports modifiers as separate line items, unlike Toast. Blau: Then map modifiers to recipe add-ons, so 'extra guac' adds the avocado cost to the parent dish instead of showing up as its own sale.
User: Should the weekly margin summary go out by text or email? Blau: Text. Your owners already respond to the price alert texts, and email gets buried under supplier newsletters.

User: The first weekly margin text went to the pilot restaurants today. Hollow Pine replied asking why their eggs went up so much. Blau: That's exactly the reaction you want. Track how many owners reply within a day as the feature's main metric.

User: Ines redesigned the onboarding so owners scan their first invoice in the first minute. Blau: Measure time to first scan and the share of trials that reach ten invoices before and after the change.
User: The car is making a grinding noise when I brake. Blau: That usually means the brake pads are worn down to the metal. Get it in this week; driving on it damages the rotors.
User: The mechanic replaced the front pads and rotors, it was $640. Blau: That's in the normal range for both. Ask them to check the rear pads at the next oil change.
User: The car registration is due on October 20th and it needs a smog check. Blau: Get the smog check done this week; the results go to the DMV electronically and you can renew online right after.

User: The tomatoes on the balcony have yellow leaves at the bottom. Blau: Lower leaves yellowing mid-summer is often uneven watering or a nitrogen shortage. Water deeply every other morning and add a little compost.
User: We got almost four pounds of cherry tomatoes this week. Blau: Roast them with garlic and freeze them flat in bags; they make a great quick pasta sauce in winter.
User: What can I plant on the balcony for fall? Blau: Lettuce, spinach, radishes and garlic all do well in Oakland's mild fall. Garlic planted in October is ready in June.

User: Biscuit has been scratching his ears a lot. Blau: Frequent ear scratching in dogs is often a yeast or ear infection, especially in floppy-eared breeds. A vet visit is worth it before it gets painful.
User: The vet said Biscuit has a yeast ear infection and gave us drops twice a day for ten days. Blau: Set two daily reminders. Finish the full course even if he seems better after a few days.
User: Biscuit's annual vaccines are due next month. Blau: I'll remember that. Book it a few weeks out; Dr. Okafor's clinic usually has a two-week wait.
User: Who can watch Biscuit while we're in Japan? Blau: Your neighbor Sofia offered in the spring. Two weeks is long, so a mix of Sofia and a sitter who stays overnight might be easier on him.
User: Our accountant wants the estimated taxes for Q3 paid by September 15th. Blau: I'll note it. Your Q2 payment was $4,200, so expect something similar unless your income changed.
User: I paid the Q3 estimated taxes, $4,350. Blau: Logged. The next estimated payment is due January 15th.

User: Can I deduct my home office if I mostly work from the studio on Telegraph? Blau: Probably not: the home office deduction needs space used regularly and exclusively for work, and your main workplace is the studio.

User: Priya and I argued about whether to build Android or the supplier price comparison next. Blau: Write down what each would do to the metric you care about most this quarter, new activated restaurants, and decide on that.

User: We decided: supplier price comparison first, Android after the seed. Priya agreed once we saw that 11 customers asked for price comparison and only 4 for Android. Blau: That's a clean, data-backed call.

User: Rosa from Little Fern called, she's opening a second location in Piedmont in March. Blau: That's great for her and for you; her second location doubles her account and makes her a strong reference for small groups.

User: Saffron Lane is thinking about cancelling because their chef left and nobody scans invoices anymore. Blau: Offer to do a two-week setup for the new chef yourself. Losing a pilot restaurant hurts more than the revenue.
User: The new chef at Saffron Lane scanned 14 invoices this week, they're staying. Blau: Good save. It's a lesson for the playbook: when a key person leaves, re-onboard their replacement right away.

User: I want to take Alex somewhere nice for our fifth anniversary on August 9th. Blau: Since you both love food, a tasting menu works. Book three to four weeks ahead and tell them about your shellfish allergy.

User: The anniversary dinner at Ferment was perfect, they made a special version of the scallop course with mushrooms for me. Blau: That's a lovely way to celebrate five years. Worth remembering for next year.
